name: Segub
title: Hiel's youngest son
summary: Segub was the youngest son of Hiel from Bethel, who died when his father rebuilt the gates of Jericho. His death fulfilled Joshua's curse against anyone who would rebuild Jericho. Segub is also mentioned as a name in the lineage of Judah through Hezron.

keyEvents.title: Joshua's Curse on Jericho
keyEvents.description: When Joshua captured Jericho, he pronounced a curse on anyone who would rebuild the city: it would cost him his firstborn to lay its foundation and his youngest son to set up its gates.

keyEvents.title: Hiel's Rebuilding of Jericho
keyEvents.description: Hiel from Bethel rebuilt Jericho during the reign of King Ahab. When he set up the gates, it cost him his youngest son Segub, exactly as Joshua had prophesied.

keyEvents.title: Fulfillment of the Prophecy
keyEvents.description: Segub's death when the city gate was raised served as a powerful reminder that God's word through Joshua came to pass, even hundreds of years after the curse was pronounced.

keyEvents.title: Segub in Judah's Genealogy
keyEvents.description: Another Segub is mentioned as the son of Hezron and daughter of Machir. This Segub became the father of Jair, who had twenty-three towns in Gilead.
